svg.title: SliceAudit: a better total can hide a worse group (synthetic demo)
svg.desc: Synthetic illustration, not a real result. Ten synthetic examples are scored by an old and a new model. The new model gets 8 of 10 right instead of 7, but the orange group drops from 4 of 4 to 2 of 4: three examples are fixed and two are broken, so the total hides the drop. SliceAudit is illustrated finding the group in one partition and checking it again in another.

g.text: The old model makes a guess for each.
Then we built a new model.
But… is it better for everyone?
Old model: 4 right. New model: only 2.
Total went up. Orange group went down.
Why didn't the total show it?
Add them up: +1. The drop disappears.
Find it. Then double-check on new data.
in one half of the data
Find model-update regressions that aggregate metrics can hide.
